connector_definition.description: The diagram's 'notched pass-through' symbol convention: a small enclosed rectangle or oval body, drawn directly on a wire bundle, with a step-notch or interlocking staircase split across its middle representing the male/female halves of a pluggable connector. Conductor/wire-color labels are preserved on both sides of the body, confirming pass-through continuity rather than any signal transformation. Two visual sub-variants were found: a simple single-notch body (CONN-001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 009, 010, 011, 012) and an interlocking multi-step staircase-split body (CONN-007, 008). Both satisfy the same engineering definition (opposing-side terminals, conductor entry+exit, inline position) and are inventoried together but their variant is recorded separately per connector.

census_methodology: Systematic visual sweep of samples/trx300ODG.png in overlapping crops, region by region, covering all 12 areas named in the task (Alarm Unit, CDI Unit, Relay cluster, Pulse Generator/Reverse Switch area, Tail-light/fuse area, Ignition Switch, Rectifier, Regulator/Rectifier, Battery/Starter Relay, Headlight harness, Indicator harness, and the connecting gaps between them), searching specifically for the notched/interlocking pass-through symbol (never for text labels or component names). Every candidate wire-mounted small symbol encountered (bullet-splice marks, diode triangles, ground bars, lamp bases, switch/sensor circles - all independently characterized in AP-DIAG-AUDIT-007/008/008B/009) was checked against the connector definition and excluded when it did not match (single-wire bullet splices and diode/fuse symbols on the headlight and indicator harnesses were the most common exclusion). The 'OPTIONAL' P/G accessory pigtail was re-confirmed excluded (one open, unterminated end).

The inventory is NOT claimed exhaustive.

pin_accounting.note: entries == exits == through-count == pin-count for all 12 connectors because every one of the 12 was directly observed to be a genuine pass-through (same number of wires enter as exit, on the opposing side, with color preserved where legible) - this equality is an observed fact for these 12, not an assumption applied uniformly. Distinct concepts kept separate throughout: 'connector pins' (physical contact positions on the connector body, counted here), 'wire endpoints' (EndpointCandidate positions in the model - a different, extraction-layer concept), 'conductor entries/exits' (raster ink observations, counted here per connector), and 'physical wires' (Wire records - a reconstructed, endpoint-to-endpoint identity that may or may not exist for the conductor on either side of a connector). None of these were conflated when producing this accounting.

representation.note: 'Partial' (1 of 12, CONN-001) means a ComponentCandidate and TerminalCandidates exist but are classified under the ordinary ComponentBoundary path, not any connector-specific model element (ConnectorCandidate=0, ConnectorTerminal=0, ConnectorBoundary=0 for all 12, no exceptions). 'Represented' (a connector with genuine connector-specific model elements) is 0 for all 12.

shape_detector_findings.conn_001_bfae05a427189376: ShapeDetector's circle-detector triggered and produced a ShapeKind::Circle region for this symbol's rounded/notched outline; ComponentCandidateClassifier mapped it to ComponentCandidateKind::CircularSymbol (component_candidate_classifier.cpp - Circle -> CircularSymbol unconditionally). No rejection occurred; it became a full ComponentCandidate.
shape_detector_findings.conn_002_through_012: No ShapeDetector-produced ComponentCandidate exists for any of these 11 locations. This audit did not instrument or modify ShapeDetector to determine the precise internal reason (no rejection-reason evidence trail is exposed by the current model for candidates that were never proposed at all, as opposed to ones proposed-then-rejected) - this is recorded as an open question for the next AP's forensic pass, not guessed at here. What IS established: ShapeDetector has no purpose-built detector for the notched/interlocking pass-through symbol family (unlike its purpose-built ChassisGround bar-pattern detector) - its available shape buckets are Circle, Rectangle-as-Enclosure, and Rectangle-as-PrimitiveSymbol, none of which is documented anywhere in the codebase as targeting this connector convention specifically. This is recorded as an architectural gap (no detector concept exists for it), consistent with, but independently re-derived from, AP-DIAG-AUDIT-009's finding for CONN-001's own shape family incompatibility.

connector_boundary_findings.architecture_trace: ComponentCandidateKind -> TerminalCandidateKind -> EndpointKind -> ConnectorCandidate -> ConnectorTerminal, per terminal_location_detector.cpp/terminal_recognizer.cpp/connector_terminal_model.cpp (traced in AP-DIAG-AUDIT-008B/009, re-confirmed unchanged here).
connector_boundary_findings.requirement: TerminalCandidateKind::ConnectorBoundary is assigned only when the owning ComponentCandidateKind is PrimitiveSymbol, which itself is only reachable from a ShapeKind::Rectangle shape that received a non-Enclosure ShapeRole.
connector_boundary_findings.compatibility_per_connector: CONN-001 has ShapeKind Circle - incompatible, confirmed in AP-DIAG-AUDIT-009. CONN-002 through CONN-012 have no ShapeKind at all (never proposed) - the compatibility question does not yet arise for them, since no candidate exists to evaluate against the requirement. If a candidate were proposed for any of them matching their actual observed shape (rounded/notched rectangle, oval, or interlocking-staircase rectangle), none of those shapes is a plain non-Enclosure Rectangle either, so the same incompatibility documented for CONN-001 would very likely recur for all 12, though this is stated as a strong inference from the observed shape family, not independently proven for each of the 11 candidateless locations.

wire_continuity_findings.conn_001: 2 topology edges, 2 physical Wires (wire-0a3ab2e5ace89210, wire-e5f7ff766561e9b7) terminate at its 2 EndpointCandidates - each Wire ends at its own endpoint there per AP-WIRE-029's hard-boundary rule; no merge made or implied.
wire_continuity_findings.conn_002_through_012: No ConductorSegment, topology node, or Wire references any of these 11 locations. Direct raster inspection confirms real, continuous, unbroken ink entering and leaving each of them on both sides - the underlying wire runs continue as ordinary conductor geometry elsewhere in the model, unbroken by any connector-boundary evidence, because no candidate exists there to anchor one.
wire_continuity_findings.crossing_rule_compliance: No finding in this audit relied on a diagonal wire, a direction change at an intersection, an X-crossing transfer, or treating a crossing as a splice/endpoint. No physical Wire identity was inferred from electrical connectivity; every observation came from raster wire-color labels and connector-symbol geometry directly.

pin_reconciliation_28_vs_46.origin_of_46: Traced directly: '46' first appears in AP-DIAG-AUDIT-008B's task prompt under 'TRX300 MANUAL ENGINEERING GROUND TRUTH', supplied as an external manual assertion, not derived from the source raster, the model, or any prior AP's own computation. No prior AP ever independently reconstructed 46 from evidence.
pin_reconciliation_28_vs_46.origin_of_28: AP-DIAG-AUDIT-009's sum of one-side pin counts across the 10 connector instances it found in a partial sweep.
pin_reconciliation_28_vs_46.this_ap_finding: This AP's more complete sweep (12 connectors) sums to 33 one-side pins - closer to, but still short of, 46, and still not reconciled under any tested convention (33 as observed, 66 if both sides of each pin are double-counted).
pin_reconciliation_28_vs_46.conclusion: 46 is NOT source-grounded by any evidence produced across AP-DIAG-AUDIT-008B, 009, or this AP. It is an externally-supplied manual count that has not been independently verified against the raster by a rigorous connector-by-connector census. Per this AP's explicit instruction, 46 is EXPLICITLY INVALIDATED as an unsupported baseline for connector-terminal reconciliation purposes - not forced to match, not assumed correct. The evidence-grounded figures available today are: 33 one-side pins across 12 located connector instances, in a sweep assessed as substantially complete but not proven exhaustive.

findings.summary: 11 of 12 located connectors have zero model representation of any kind (no ComponentCandidate); the one exception (CONN-001) is represented via the ordinary ComponentBoundary terminal path, not any connector-specific element, and its own ShapeKind (Circle) is architecturally incompatible with the current ConnectorBoundary->PrimitiveSymbol requirement.
findings.downstream_consequence: Confirms and extends AP-DIAG-AUDIT-009's finding across the complete 12-connector inventory: this is not a critical defect against current production behavior (0 ConnectorCandidates was already the accepted, understood baseline), but it is the central evidence gap a future connector-representation AP must close.

recommended_next_ap: A ShapeDetector forensic instrumentation AP (audit-only, no modification) that traces, for each of the 12 CONN-* locations individually, the exact internal reason no ComponentCandidate is proposed (candidate detector triggered vs. not, rejection condition if any, relevant threshold values) - closing the specific gap this AP explicitly left open (Section 'shape_detector_findings') - before any connector architecture (new ComponentCandidateKind, ConnectorBoundary re-keying, or pin/pass-through model) is designed.
